goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:124 — Same `forEach(async ...)` fire-and-forget pattern as vital/lib/reschedule.ts:124, causing unhandled promise rejections and ordering races

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (and similarly in vital). Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, the `await getCalendar(...)` and subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` promises are not awaited by the surrounding `try` block, leading to fire-and-forget behavior, potential unhandled promise rejections, and races where `Reschedule` can finish before deletions complete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: trpc/.../bookings.tsx:553 — forEach(async ...)` callback is not awaited, so the async work runs detached from the enclosing function, risking unhandled rejections and race conditions with later logic

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })`. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the returned promises from `deleteEvent` are not awaited by the surrounding function. This detaches the async work, risking unhandled rejections and allowing later logic to run before deletions complete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-store/index.ts — import()` calls execute eagerly at module scope instead of lazily on demand, defeating the intended benefit of switching to dynamic imports

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the object literal initializes each entry as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`, etc. Because these `import()` expressions are evaluated during module initialization, they will start loading immediately when `app-store/index.ts` is imported, rather than being deferred until a specific app is actually accessed. This undermines the intended “lazy on demand” behavior of switching to dynamic imports, but is primarily a performance/architecture issue rather than a functional correctness bug.
